newsitem.title: ITALY: Boss says Mafia wanted to kill Italy's Di Pietro.
newsitem.headline: Boss says Mafia wanted to kill Italy's Di Pietro.

text.p: Captured Mafia boss Giovanni Brusca has told investigators that he wanted to kill former graft-busting magistrate Antonio Di Pietro in 1992, Italian judicial sources said on Friday.

They said Brusca told Florence magistrates earlier this month that he had floated the idea within Cosa Nostra of killing Di Pietro as a way to take the spotlight off Sicily after the crime group murdered two star magistrates there in 1992.

Giovanni Falcone and Paolo Borsellino were killed in Palermo in May and July 1992, just as Di Pietro was spearheading the vast "Clean Hands" corruption probes in Milan that brought down Italy's political old guard.
The plan to kill Di Pietro was never carried out partly because Brusca was too busy with other crimes, the sources said.

Di Pietro, who quit the magistrature in 1994 for unexplained reasons, stepped down last week as public works minister after coming under investigation himself for alleged malpratice. He dismisses the allegations as a vendetta.
Brusca, a 32-year-old mobster with one of the most violent reputations in Sicily, was arrested last May and has been "cooperating" with police since August.
Some experts suspect he may be a "false turncoat" and his testimony is being closely studied by investigators.
The sources said Brusca made his comments about Di Pietro to Florence magistrates questioning him about bombings that rocked Rome, Florence and Milan in 1993, killing 10 people.
Brusca and Mafia bosses Salvatore Riina and Leoluca Bagarella went on trial in Florence earlier this month charged with masterminding the bombings.
